utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are present. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Ms. Condon and Mr. Ostojic. I think that's about it. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Yes. Are there any preliminaries before we bring in Mr. Rodic? Okay. I understand that some of you at least wish to address the Chamber later on after Mr. Rodic has concluded his testimony, and you will have, of course, the opportunity to do so, as much time as you require. Could you usher in Mr. Rodic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, to you, Mr. Rodic. Welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for keeping your appointment with us. I'm sure that we'll finish with your testimony today and so you will be able to go back home immediately after if you so desire. I'll swear you in again. Madam Usher is going to hand to you the text of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please read it out aloud. You know what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Vanderpuye was halfway through his cross-examination when we suspended your testimony last time. He will now continue and finish. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for coming back. Mr. President is right; I'm just about halfway through my examination of you, so please bear with me while we get through it. First of all, I'd like to ask you, did you discuss your testimony or your report with anyone during the time that you'd been away from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you speak to anybody regarding the subject matter of your testimony more generally?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant I didn't discuss that subject during the break, but I did discuss some arrangements for my travel to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the last we left off we were talking about a map,?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if I could have, please, 65 ter number 1468. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see that on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. It's a section of the map of the area that I worked on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go down to the area of Veliki Zep. It should be on the bottom. There it is. That's -- that's fine.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's it. That's Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And now, is this the same section of the map that was shown to you by Mr. Zivanovic a couple of days before you testified last?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the location of the station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, because I interrupt my colleague. But I would offer this map to the witness so he could see it much -- more clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any objection to that, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no objection. In fact I would just like to identify that for the record, if it has an assigned number other than -- other than what's displayed in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if you would please first show it to Mr. Vanderpuye to -- okay. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The end radio relay station Vlasenica is shown on both maps in the same place. The frequencies between the end relay station Vlasenica and Veliki Zep are identical on the map, 7805.00 megahertz, and 834.250 megahertz. The location of Veliki Zep is the same on both maps, so it's radio relay direction R-800 between Veliki Zep and Vlasenica, between the command of the Drina corps in Vlasenica and the radio relay knob in -- hub, sorry, in Veliki Zep. We see SMC direction to Veliki Zep, but I don't see it on the monitor. If you can move the map towards the end point, it's this direction, SMC. Then move the map to north-east, but -- but we don't see the full picture, but I know from the map, the full one, that it first showed relay communications, that it's the direction towards Cer, so the 120-channel radio relay axis Veliki Zep-Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell from the map that you have in front of you that's just been provided to you whether or not it is drawn from this map that is in e-court now? And if you can't, that's fine too.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what I've seen so far, that's the map. That's the right map. But I would also like to see the one that I analysed, the other directions, Zvornik-Gucevo, and Gucevo-Cer, and Veliki Zep-Bratunac. I would like to cover them all so I am absolutely sure of my data.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you review any map before you testified last other than this map that's now before you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed this map over two or three days when I came first to The Hague and that's the information I have, the basis on that map. I did not receive any other information subsequently. This direction going towards Bratunac, RRU-1, it's not so clear on the monitor, 252.275 megahertz, although megahertz is not written here. That's one frequency, since there is reception and/inaudible/should have been two, as on this map. Then on the same line we see RRU-800 towards Bratunac with the frequency of 705.00. I don't see it on the map. We should move it to the right. I suppose that's the other pair of frequencies, 805 MHz towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't need for you to compare every point in the map. I just want to know, frankly, if you've seen the larger map prior to testifying the last time -- prior to testifying the last time you were in court. That's the map that's on the computer. Have you seen that total map before?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. I believe that's the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So before you testified on the last date, you were shown the -- the map in total. And if we could just zoom out for a moment so you can see the entire map. All right. So prior to testifying last, you actually did have an opportunity to see this entire map; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on that map you were able to see the locations that are indicated for Vlasenica; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not very clear, but I believe it's Vlasenica, Veliki Zep, Cer, Kuce -- Gucevo, and Zvornik. That is the axis that I analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So that particular route as divided by those four paths are clearly indicated on this map which you reviewed before you testified last; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of their specific locations relative to the interception posts, those locations are accurate, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time I stated that the position as drawn on this map, the position of Vlasenica is not exactly as I stated in my analysis. Maybe it's a purely graphic matter. And the same goes for Zvornik. They are a bit different from my analysis and my information: and the position of the nodes Veliki Zep, Cer and Gucevo, is the same as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just zoom in on the right-hand side of the map. Yes, right there. Could you move that towards the middle please? Yes. The location where Cer is. On the right-hand side in the middle of the map. Is it possible to centre that? All the way on the right.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Other way. Yes. Okay. Do you see where it says Ka Avali on the right-hand side? If you could just blow that up. The location on the right-hand side of the computer at this time, that represents the location of Cer, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. That indicates that there is a RRU-800 device that operates on that line towards Gucevo; right? Do you see -- do you see the number 800 on that line?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see 200 and 800 on this, and on the schematics that I had, and according to the data of the Drina Corps, it was the route of -- for RRU-800, Cer-Gucevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go down from Gucevo -- there it is in the middle of the screen just about, towards Zvornik and if you could blow that up, please. Okay, you have to come down a little bit on the screen. No, other way.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see the line from Gucevo to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this route. It has one frequency, 123 -- it's not quite clear. 823.00 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's a frequency that corresponds to a RRU-800 device, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It corresponds to the range in which RRU is capable of working on that route. I don't know whether the transmission is from Gucevo or from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, consistent with the path that you analyse which indicates on it that that particular path is -- is communication along a RRU-800 device. Isn't that right? That's what's in your report.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the route Zvornik-Gucevo, connection was established with RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so with respect to the paths from Zvornik to Gucevo, Gucevo to Cer, Cer to Veliki Zep, and Veliki Zep to Vlasenica, this map indicates all of the correct devices that were in place according to your report, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were devices that were in operation on the route Vlasenica-Zvornik, or vice versa, Zvornik-Vlasenica, and only the Vlasenica-Zvornik and Zvornik-Vlasenica communications took place along these radio-relay routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question is --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. On Veliki Zep, it was possible to connect onto communications from the Main Staff of the VRS at Veliki Zep, as well as the connection with Bratunac established with RRU-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question is whether or not those devices are accurately depicted on this map as concerns the specific route that you analysed, and they are, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for schematics, the multiplex devices are missing there, from which we could see the capacities of these communications. From the data of the Drina Corps, I know that on the Zvornik-Gucevo route, and an intermediate station existed on Gucevo to Cer, there were 12 telephone channels. As for the relay devices, it is depicted correctly in the sense that the route was operated by a RRU-800. I do not claim that the frequencies used on those routes as depicted here are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm asking about the devices. We can agree on that; right? That the devices in terms of whether it's a RRU-800 or RRU-1 device along the particular paths is accurately depicted in this map. Yes?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. On the route Zvornik-Gucevo, there were a couple of RRU-800 devices. On the Gucevo-Cer, there were also a couple of devices RRU-800. On the Cer-Veliki Zep route, there was a double transmitter, a pair of SMCC devices and on Veliki Zep-Vlasenica route there was a pair of RRU-800 devices as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you didn't have an opportunity to review this particular map until after you'd written your report; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I looked at the map here when I came here. Two or three days before the 23rd when I appeared here as an expert witness for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't have the benefit of this map when you concluded in your report that the ABiH did not have information relating to the radio relay route that you analysed; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's why I drew some of my conclusions based on the orientation of the antennas when we intercepted the conversations, because these antennas from the physical locations of north and south were not directed towards the facilities that we are talking about here, especially not towards Veliki Zep where there was a strong concentration of communication links which is visible from the angles, i.e., the azimuth, that were represented in their reports for certain intercepted conversations. It arises from that, and it is only logical, that they simply did not provide for the optimum direction of their antenna system towards the facility that was the object of interception.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecutor has asked the witness if his conclusions would have been the same if he had had this map. I think this question is relevant only if this map dates from the year 1995, that is, from the relevant times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your observation on that Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it's a completely invalid objection particularly to the extent that I haven't asked any question based upon that other than whether the witness had the opportunity to review it prior to drawing his -- drawing the conclusions that were contained in his report. My question goes to the accuracy of the report as opposed to the accuracy of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecutor has asked the witness whether his conclusions would have been the same if he had had the map, and I believe that it is relevant with regard to the fact whether this map existed in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't agree with you, Madam Fauveau. Whether it existed or not in 1995, it's not relevant. The whole question boils down to if he had this map available at the time he was drawing up his report, his report would have been the same or would have been different. So -- and I think in any case he's now been told that this map doesn't go back to 1995 in any case. So let's -- let's proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could I have please 5D00123 on e-court, please. If you could just page down to the bottom of this. I think there's also an English translation. Is there a translation that -- it's coming up or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see that in front of you, Mr. Rodic? This is a report from the --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see part of the document, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. One moment. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: May we see the date of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I was just going to page up so that you could see the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, both of you. We see the date now, and it's 8/8/1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This isn't being broadcast, is it? It is being broadcast. Okay. I think we -- I think maybe we ought not to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, we don't have a hard copy of that map, and we all think that it will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: A hard copy of 1468?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. Not now, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll bring it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see this document in front of you, Mr. Rodic, that it's dated 8 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just go down to the bottom of this document. And at the bottom of this document do you see an area which relates to the locations and code-names relative to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are you familiar with those code-names and those locations?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for the locations that were of interest to my analysis, I'm familiar with them. I was not interested in any others. As for the code-names, they didn't mean anything to me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just page up to the first paragraph of this document. Do you see in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For your information, there is no broadcast -- or was it broadcast? It was broadcast. So we have to redact that part because it shows the site, one of the sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just leave it in our hands. We'll deal with that. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, this document is in fact an order, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says. The radio surveillance order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there's a specific instruction to the radio intercept units to direct their antennas towards Zvornik, Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, and Srebrenica, Bratunac and Vlasenica. Do you see that, corresponding frequencies?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, but I cannot interpret the same way you are doing it. It says here that radio surveillance should be carried out on the frequencies 784.700 megahertz, Zvornik-Vlasenica-Han Pijesak. That's one frequency and these are three facilities, or three radio relay axes. I am not able to say about this radio frequency Zvornik, Vlasenica and Han Pijesak are geographic at different coordinates. In other words, I cannot tie this frequency either to Zvornik or to Vlasenica or to Han Pijesak, and especially in view of the light where Han Pijesak is. According to what I have Han Pijesak is a place between Vlasenica and Crna Rijeka and Veliki Zep, and I don't have Han Pijesak in my analysis because as far as I know no radio communication worked there. The second frequency, 654.000 megahertz, it says the radio surveillance should be done on route Srebrenica-Bratunac-Vlasenica. As radio relay person, when I take this territory into consideration, if the person who issued this order, that thought that this was a communication that was established, I did not analyse it, but I can confirm that due to the nature of the obstacles, the geographical obstacles -- obstacles, this radio relay route cannot function as such. In my view, this is a very undefined order, very vague order. One frequency with two routes and three facilities, it is very dubious as to which route would this frequency relate to. This is my approach. I'm not entering into the matter of the style of order issuing and the way the orders were drafted in the BiH army. I'm approaching the subject from the point of view of a radio relay expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, your analysis of the radio relay route in question, from Vlasenica to Zvornik, was based upon a report that you looked at, which was dated in 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you give me the number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The number is 04314791. You have it right there in front of you. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it in the attachments 12 and 13. This is a report of the Drina Corps command to the Main Staff concerning the radio relay communications. They tell the Drina Corps, and the date is 2nd October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. In fact, one of the frequencies that's referred to in that document corresponds to the operation of a RRU-800 device between Vlasenica and Veliki Zep. That's under Article 2 in that document; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under item 2 in the document, as part of the attachment 12, so, it deals with the work and the time route Veliki Zep, 24-channel, right, the direction Veliki Zep, the Drina Corps, i.e., Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And one of the corresponding frequencies on that path is 680 megahertz; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 680 megahertz, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if I could have P02822 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We're not broadcasting, are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher -- Madam Registrar? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. First you see the date of this document. This is 18th November 1993.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see this is a document that originated in the southern site, or at least refers to the southern site; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the southern site, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could please go to -- it's the ERN number is -- ends 649, so six pages forward. If we could go down to the bottom of the page. Now, with reference to this document, sir, do you see an indication in the document as to the frequencies that are active? Well, maybe I can direct your attention to it. In the document, you see in the direction of Vlasenica, an azimuth of 115 degrees. Do you see that -- do you see that on that document?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, above the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you see that one of the active frequencies within the range of the operating RRU-800 device is 680. That's on the left column, second from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: According to your information, based upon the 1993 Drina Corps order, that call responds exactly to the frequency that was in operation along that specific route; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the frequency.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that is missing is the fact that there were two frequencies on the route from Vlasenica to Veliki Zep or from Veliki Zep to Vlasenica. So this is not very well-defined. The second undefined thing is whether this is from Veliki Zep. I'm talking about the document that is in front of me. In the document that I used, that frequency was from Veliki Zep towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, what's depicted on this particular document is that it's from that direction and it corresponds to the frequency that you say was in operation based upon a 1993 Drina Corps order; correct?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. According to the frequency plan, this frequency was operational from Veliki Zep towards Vlasenica. This was according to a Drina Corps order. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So in 1995, it's apparent that the ABiH had information concerning the frequencies in operation that you claim were in operation since 1993, at least along that particular path. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this particular frequency, I would say that that is the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did none of the documents that you analysed concerning the intercepts that you looked at actually contained that specific frequency? Isn't that true? In 1995.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True. But my calculation shows that they could not, here at the southern site, irrespective of the frequency, not even with the equipment they had, due to the relation of the angles of the radiation diagrams – they could not intercept any conversations on that frequency. Look at my calculation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your conclusion, and correct me if I'm wrong, is that the ABiH had the information concerning an active frequency since 1993 that you claim was in effect and in operation in 1995, and yet not one intercept that you examined in relation to your analysis corresponds to a frequency that they've known about for two years. That's your testimony? Is that what your conclusion is?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents that I reviewed, that I had at my disposal, that would be the case, which I confirm. No document that I reviewed with regard to this frequency --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. This document wasn't one of the documents you reviewed before you made your report. Fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In fact, during the course of preparing your report you came across no document that actually indicates that the frequencies you believed to have been in operation in 1995 were those frequencies that were in operation in 1993; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed the documents that are specified in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there's no document specified in your analysis establishing the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for a minute? It's a problem of a double-ended question, the previous series of questions. You asked this document was wasn't one of the documents, and at the end you added, "Fair to say?" The witness said no. No to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Thank you. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This was not a document that you reviewed prior to preparing your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He said ne. I could hear him clearly say ne.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the only document that you were able to find concerning the frequencies that were in operation in 1995 is in fact a document that is dated in 1993.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the documents originating from the Drina Corps, the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've reviewed no document or seen any document establishing what the frequencies in operation were in 1995 that's actually dated in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the frequency, the answer would be no. When we're talking about frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've reviewed no document prior to preparing your report which indicates that the frequencies were not changed between 1993 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the radio relay connections, I didn't. As for the other types of connections, I saw a number of documents regarding various radio systems that changed very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And part of your analysis you reviewed the technical aspects of the equipment that was used by the ABiH; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I could collect as data, yes, and what I considered sufficient for the level of the analysis that I was involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as part of your review of the technical aspects of the equipment, you reviewed a list of equipment, an inventory as it were.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had documents for the north and the south sites with jobs, pieces of equipment for -- at various workplaces and some other specifications specifying other equipment, i.e., the entire inventory for both these sites which is auxiliary to radio equipment, antennas, recording devices, and similar equipment which I did not specify in my analysis because it is auxiliary equipment. I just provide short comments about those in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, in particular in your analysis you provided some comments about equipment that you were not sure what it was used for; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular, you referred in your report to the use of a converter in the capacity of interception of one of the sites; do you recall having done that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is on page 11 of my report. A converter which converts a signal from a 150 to 18 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in your report you indicated that you didn't know what it was used for; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the interception of conversations on RRU-800 and RRU-1. I don't see a reason for this converter, because this converter converts the frequency of 150 MHz to 18 MHz, and the frequency area of a RRU-1, which is a lower area, is 235 to 270 MHz, and for RRU-800, 610-960 MHz. So this converter cannot accept frequencies of these two pieces of equipment and convert it into a lower frequency that would lend itself to analysis. I believe for that it is pointless for the interception of conversations by these two pieces of equipment, and I don't know why it should be an accompanying piece of equipment together with the RRU-800 and RRU-1. And especially the SMCC equipment which is within the range of 4.4 to 5 gigahertz, which is far beyond this range.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Fair enough. You made the same observation of a different converter, S042; that's also in your report, right? And you indicated that it had no clear role. That's in section 5.2.1b of your report.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's in item b.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your observations of equipment that you couldn't make out what it was used for, did you consider the possibility that that equipment could have been modified and used in a function other than it was intended for?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any information about any modification, because in that report the purpose of the equipment is not specified, and it's not specified which frequency area is input, which is output, there is no sensitivity indicated, or the level of output. So from those elements that I had I could not analyse much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a minute. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to have to interrupt the witness. I believed that he had finished. In fact, there is a little mistake in the transcript that could be important. It's on page 19, line 7, RRU-800 was mentioned twice, and the first one should have been RRU-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that, Madam Fauveau, but let's make it a practice, if it's something that has to do with the transcript, just let us see that you need to address us, but you should wait until the witness has finished answering the question if he happens to have already started. But this time I quite understand, because even I understood that he had finished his -- his answer basically. Let's finish your answer first, Witness. You had started saying, "I didn't have any information about any modification, because in that report the purpose of the equipment is not specified and it's not specified which frequency area is input, which is output. There is no sensitivity indicated or output. So from those I could not analyse much." And you were about to tell us something more. If you could continue now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, quite simply in the report dealing with these workplaces, there is no rationale indicated for what the equipment was used and what the interceptors were using so I couldn't make any assumptions there. And the primary object of my analysis was the receiver. So I followed the signal from RRU-800 to the entry into the receiver. What happened later was irrelevant to me. Why? Because in my calculations I indicated that if the receiver was not receiving a signal, or was not receiving it in good quality, then it was irrelevant what later happened in the technology, the analysis of signals, and whatever else they used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go to the correction or mistake that Madam Fauveau indicated. We are at line 19 -- page 19, line 7. And the correction is to the effect that although we have in the transcript RRU-800 mentioned twice, the first one should be RRU-1. Is that correct, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that correct, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. So there are two different devices. RRU-800 is one of them. What I said about the converters is that they are not necessary for that range at all. In fact, they cannot accept the signal from that – from those devices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You know, my question was, Mr. Rodic, whether or not you considered that. That's about as simple as the question can be, and the answer should be a yes or no. Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I considered the converter S042. Should I go back to it and remind myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Whether or not you considered the possibility it could have been modified?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about with respect to the antennas used?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assume such things, and I never found in their reports anywhere that they modified something or to which purpose they might have modified this converter S042.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you never reviewed any statements, testimony of anybody or operator involved in the actual processing of these intercepts; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not take into account any previous testimony or witness statement except maybe one that I will deal with later. None were presented to me. And that one that I mentioned is not linked to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, of the intercepts that you actually looked at that are indicated in your report, do you know whether or not you considered all of the 213 intercepts that have been offered in this case from those particular locations?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took into account the intercepts for which I had some background information, the frequency, with which antenna it was intercepted. I took into account the intercepts of which I had technical data about the process of interception. I don't know how many documents were available, but I selected the intercepts that are here in my file, in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that in your analysis the number of intercepts that correspond to the intercepts that have been offered in this case of the 213 is about 83? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean included here, 83? No, I did not reckon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you -- did you calculate in your report how many of those intercepts, the ones that you -- that are actually -- that correspond to the intercepts that have been offered in this case, how many of those intercepts actually originated with the 2nd Corps units whose equipment you analysed?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Are you aware that in the northern site there was more than one interception unit in operation in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the reports, I see that there was this one unit, and there was also the State Security Service of Tuzla. Those are the only things I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you didn't actually analyse the equipment that was used by the state security services of Tuzla in your report, did you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to see in any of the documents what kind of equipment they had or to analyse it. There was only one background document which told me that they had a rotor -- a rotator in the northern location. It was not in operation yet, and then it was stolen. It was actually a security report speaking about the detection of the perpetrator. I don't know if they were an operative unit, but in some way they were present with their equipment. I don't even remember the date because it was irrelevant to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But you're aware that they had equipment that was different from the equipment that you actually analysed. Yes?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know? It was not stated anywhere. They did not describe the kind of equipment they had in the information I had. In other words, I don't know because I did not have such documentation. And their reports are very peculiar. They have a different format from the other formats used by the BH army. They are worded in general terms without indicating who the participants in the conversation are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So your report in general does not address the viability or possibility of interception by the state security services operating out of the north facility at all; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only thing that I mentioned in my prior testimony is that frequency, 630 megahertz. In their reports, it was stated that it was used somewhere in the area of Sarajevo, Lukavica, Rajlovac, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you're also aware that in your report consideration of the intercepts that you looked at you attributed certain intercepts that were created by the state security services to the intercepts that were secured in the southern facility. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. I cannot tell now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot differentiate now between various numbers and who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, when you organised your report did you take into consideration when you were attributing the possibility of intercepts to each of these two locations what unit was actually intercepting from those locations?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my report the focus is on which frequency exists on a certain location. Everything else is auxiliary. Which unit, whether it was the south or northern location, or whether it was state security or somebody else. The focus is on the fact that a certain frequency was subject to listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did you consider the fact that there was yet another, a third unit operating from the northern facility, independently of the equipment that you analysed? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? I can assume that there was a unit in the air, that it was perhaps outside the borders of the area controlled by the BH army. I can assume anything, but my job was to analyse what the BH army was doing. I can make various assumptions, but I don't want to because it would be less than serious. I have some knowledge about how this is done. A third person can intercept certain conversations, and they can be noted in notebooks and transcripts can exist, but this is something I can state only in general terms. I cannot go into deeper analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So the answer is no, you didn't consider the fact that there was another unit operating from the northern facility in terms of your analysis.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my analysis, I did not take that into account because I did not have any documents to corroborate the existence of such units, except knowing that the state security from Tuzla was also intercepting conversations. I knew that they had some equipment for it, but apart from their presence in the northern location, I cannot confirm that they operated from another location as well. It's not in any of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you didn't consider the incidents where the frequencies that were monitored with respect to the possibility of interception were the same among all three units, did you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that they recorded the same conversations on the same frequencies, if I understood you correctly. You mean the same transcripts were made by the same three intercepting parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is whether or not you considered that when you looked at these intercepts that you analysed. Did you look to see whether or not there were incidents in which all three independent units recorded on the same frequency, the same purported location? Did you look for that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not look for it because I was primarily interested in whether on the frequencies that I knew, with communications between Vlasenica and Zvornik, interception was technically possible in view of the receiving frequencies. I did not go deeper into analysis or comparison. Maybe I should have done. Maybe that's a failure. Maybe I would have noticed some discrepancy in contents, but I didn't analyse that bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the intercepts that you actually did look at, those 83 intercepts, you can't tell us now how many of those intercepts actually relate to the route that you analysed, can you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not one. Except that those two frequencies were unknown, and they are a possibility. But they are only two out of 16 frequencies, and I don't have insight into two frequencies between Cer and Gucevo where possibly two out of 16 were from the northern or southern location.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, what my question is, I suppose, is: Is it possible that of the intercepts you examined that relatively few of them actually purport to have been captured along the route that you analysed? Did you analyse that possibility?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said there were 16 different frequencies that were listened to from the northern and southern location, and there were only two unknown frequencies, the receiving and transmitting one between Gucevo and Cer. That alone tells us how many other problematic frequencies existed, namely the intercepts I introduced in my analysis, of course according to available documentation and especially the plan of frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, the plan that you're talking about actually doesn't contain two central frequencies to the route that you analysed; right? Doesn't that tell you that the plan that you analyse is incomplete? All right.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because it was within the jurisdiction of the Drina Corps to monitor routes between Vlasenica to Veliki Zep and from Zvornik to Gucevo. Other routes, Veliki Zep-Cer and Veliki Zep-Gucevo were within the jurisdiction of the Main Staff. That's why the Drina Corps did not report to the Main Staff about these frequencies, because they were not within their area. That's why they're not in the documents of the Drina Corps. You can see that also from other documents dealing with securing the equipment covering those radio relay routes, those communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have documentation from -- from Gucevo to Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have frequencies Gucevo-Zvornik and Zvornik-Gucevo, because that's a radio relay route with which the Zvornik Brigade relied on Gucevo, and it had to have that information because the transmitting frequency towards Gucevo was the frequency on the RRU-800 in Zvornik, and the receiving frequency in Zvornik was the same as the transmitting frequency from Gucevo. That's why they have to have in their file both frequencies but not Gucevo towards Cer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also don't have the frequencies for the back-up RRU-800 device that you say was operating between Veliki Zep and Cer; right? That's not in the document that you -- that you referred to, is it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no frequencies. That equipment was in preparation. The purpose of the equipment was to be back-up when SMC for some reason is out of use, so that the most -- selectively, the most essential communications between Veliki Zep towards Cer, and Gucevo and Zvornik can be relayed. So in principle, when you plan a route like that you secure a workplace for it at the facility and antenna, and you wait until the moment when it's necessary to use it, and that's when you determine the frequency, because that switch can take place suddenly, but it may not take place at all for many years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, you have no information whatsoever when, if at all, that back-up RRU-800 device between Cer and Veliki Zep was ever in operation. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994 it was active when there were NATO airstrikes on Veliki Zep. So the SMC route Veliki Zep-Cer was not in operation, and that's when the back-up of RRU-800 was used. I don't have information about the frequencies, but I personally was involved in enabling the SMC route, and when the SMC route was enabled again then this back-up route was switch off, after covering the major communications between Veliki Zep and Cer for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We're talking about within the period of your analysis; right? Within the period of your analysis you have no information whether or when that particular unit was in operation; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radio relay route covered by RRU-800 between Cer and Veliki Zep had no need to operate because the capacity, as I showed in my analysis, was realised between those two facilities using the SMC, which has the double capacity of RRU-800, even when the latter is working at maximum capacity. It was senseless to use them both at the same time. There also existed a secure communication route which I did not include in my analysis because I did not have any information that there were any communications from cryptographically protected routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The SMC device you're talking about is the one that you went to go fix in August of 1995. That's what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes. Yes. The device, yes. But I didn't go to repair it. It was regular technical check-up and assistance so that the whole system including the SMC, the RRU-800 and all the multiplex devices that existed there would be brought up to a good level. And I already said that the VRS did not have the staff for that, and that's why a team, including me, came to improve it. It was not out of operation. It's a double transmitter and receiver, unlike the others. It has two radio devices, and it's very robust. So when one radio is not working, the other one is, and the communication is of good quality. But it's always better to have two transmissions over two radios on SMC, and the job of that team was to bring it up to snuff technologically, so that it can function as envisaged. It was not broken down; it was a scheduled maintenance and assistance, and it was purely by chance that we found ourselves on that day at the facility at Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, your report doesn't account for four potentially active RRU-800 frequencies.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four. You mean two. Four are mentioned on the route Vlasenica-Veliki Zep route, Zvornik and Gucevo, but there is no reference to Gucevo-Cer. Whereas on the route Cer-Veliki Zep, there was the SMC, which is not within the frequency range of RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that there was a back-up RRU-800 device that could operate between Cer and Veliki Zep. That much is accurate; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means, and I repeat --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want a yes or no, if I could, please.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The piece of equipment has its place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the preparation without any specific frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... Already answered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where? Where? Where did he answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see exact page, but he was asked about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he can -- the question, previous question -- let me freeze this. "Mr. Rodic, your report doesn't account for four potentially active RRU-800 frequencies." And he answered -- the first answer was, "Four. You mean two. Four are mentioned on the route Vlasenica-Veliki Zep route, Zvornik and Gucevo, but there is no reference to Gucevo-Cer, whereas on the route Cer-Veliki Zep there was the SMC which is not within the frequency range of RRU-800." And then there was the next question where you interrupted: "Sir, you testified that there was a back-up RRU-800 device that could operate between Cer and Veliki Zep. That much is accurate; right?" And then your -- he started answering, and we had your interruption -- or intervention. But the thing is it's being put to him that indeed he has already made such a statement, but he is being asked to clarify. So let's continue. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 29, line 9 up to line 13, the witness answered the question, since he stated as follows: "[In English] The radio relay route covered by RRU-800 between Cer and Veliki Zep had no need to operate, because as I showed in my analysis, was realised between those two facilities using the SMC."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. She could be right. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question to him was whether it could operate as distinguished from whether it was in operation, and I think that's an important distinction in light of the fact that the witness is claiming to have personal knowledge that that it was never in operation during the period of time which he conducted his analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very well. I think we can proceed. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He answered this question too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where? Where did he answer it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the same place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. At the same place he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was [indiscernible] route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He "had no need to operate because as I showed in my analysis between those two facilities using SMC which has double capacity of RRU-800, even when the latter is working at maximum capacity. It was senseless to use them both at the same time. There also existed the secure communication route which I did not include in my analysis because I did not have any information that there were any communication from cryptographically protected routes." Yeah, but the question is more precise than that, whether he has knowledge, actually, that the RRU-800 was also used in spite of your conclusion that there was -- it would have been senseless to -- to use it. Yes. What you testified earlier on is your conclusion, your opinion based on your expertise that it wouldn't have made sense using the SMC and also the RRU-800, but can you exclude that the RRU-800 was indeed made use of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I exclude that possibility. The SMC has a five-time bigger capacity than the RRU-800. Not double the capacity, but five times the capacity of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's your witness, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've overpassed the time for our break. We'll have a 25-minute break, and we'll continue after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rodic. You just indicated, I think, last before we took the break that you exclude the possibility that the RRU-800 device, the back-up device on the path between Cer and Veliki Zep was in use during the period of your -- the period of time that your analysis covers. That's between June and August of 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't see the logic. If a 120-channel system is operational between Cer and Veliki Zep, I don't see a logic of a RRU-800 with up to 24 channels working at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. That's not part of the frequency plan that you reviewed from the Drina Corps of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no frequency for that path in the frequency plan that I reviewed for my analysis, and that is actually part of my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you didn't -- you didn't obtain any other frequency plan other than that, the 1993 one from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any other frequency plan, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you ask for any such frequency plan for 1995?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for all documents relative to that period, and I received what I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So your analysis was conducted in light of the documents that you had at your disposal and no other documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there is no document that's included with your report that you otherwise relied on directly establishing the frequencies that were in use in 1995 during the period of your analysis; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to frequencies, there's none. There are other documents that I reviewed, quite a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Part of your analysis that's concluded in your report relates to having reviewed certain scouting or searching reports that were made up by the ABiH. That's in section 6 of your report.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I analysed reports on the search of frequencies. Those are frequencies that the BiH army searched at these two sites, but they are not linked to any documents, or at least I did not find such documents about the intercepted communications. They just searched the frequencies and their quality and that's what is stated in the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So with respect to that aspect of your report, that analysis has really nothing to do with the documents that you in fact analysed concerning the intercepts -- the intercepts that are appended to your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't establish a link for two reasons. Firstly, what I included contains a frequency, an azimuth, and a time. Here there is a time, an azimuth, but it does not contain any contents, and I don't think that the purpose of that was to record intercepted conversations but just to record the spectrum, i.e., the frequencies that appear under a certain angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to the angles you analysed, those angles corresponded to a direction that was westerly from these facilities; isn't that true? The interception facilities, so that I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can tell it's clear from the north side, 240 degrees would be almost opposite to the facilities that I analysed. For example, this is under item 6.1. Further on, under 6.2, again from the location north, this is 286 degrees. Again, this is even less favourable angle with regard to the facilities that remained on a different side to the maximum direction of the antenna where the reception of the intercepted conversation is the worst. 274 degrees from the location south, this is again a westward direction, and the facilities are mostly located in the east or in the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so the conclusion that you drew as a result of analysing these searching or scouting reports is effectively that when the antenna is turned opposite to the direction in which the radio relay route is, that the reception is worse than when the antenna is turned toward that route. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see this from any of the diagrams of the antenna direction. We can look at the enclosure 30. If the antenna is turned --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask it in a general way, because --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms this is the least favourable direction. I have the very correct diagrams of these antennas. There is a slight variation. There is less favourable direction and extremely unfavourable direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to the intercepts that you actually looked at, none of those intercepts correspond to any one of those scouting directions, that is either 240 degrees, 274 degrees, or 286 degrees. That's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, because I have stated exactly under item 10 that these intercepted conversations were done on the 135 degrees and 170 degrees of the antenna angle, or as they said it, from the south-east or south direction. Based on that, for the known frequencies, I carried out my calculations under item 11. For these specific frequencies for these two facilities, for the frequencies that I had in the BiH army documents, I carried out my calculations and represented them in the tables under item 11 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your calculations, it is true that the ability to receive a given signal depends upon the angle in which it's transmitted and the angle from which it's received; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely right, because an antenna has a diagram of emission, and in addition to the optical radio visibility and the distance between the two points in addition to other parameters, the efficiency of the antenna depends on that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So the ability to hear a given frequency or receive one varies depending upon the angle that a receiving antenna or a transmitting antenna is turned; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Given the pattern of emission from any one antenna, either transmitting or receiving, the angle that the reception is -- from which there is reception can drastically affect the ability to receive a transmission; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very drastically. The angles can be such that the antenna cannot receive any signal, because it falls within the minimum range of antenna's reception, which is more than 30 decibels. This is a thousand times lesser strength of reception at the receiver.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So given that, it's very important to be precise in the angles from which -- from which reception can be gained in terms of -- in terms of analysing the ability to receive a given transmission?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You concluded based upon your review of the intercepts that are referred to in your report that the direction of 180 degrees, rather, the direction of south corresponded precisely to 180 degrees; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the south site it says in the reports 180 degrees, and for the north it says south. And since this south can be undefined, but I believe that south in -- in respect of north would be best represented by 180 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's fair enough, but that's an assumption that you made, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An assumption, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you also assume that when you saw the direction of south-east that that meant -- that meant a degree direction of 135 degrees precisely; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the south site, then the operator states in the documents 135 degrees. In terms of the north site, he says south-east and I took 135 degrees as the most correct or accurate orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Fair enough. But that's an assumption that you made, isn't it, because the exact degree angle is not indicated on the document; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not indicated, but I put it down to the style of writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You can agree that where the document indicates a direction of south or south-east, it does not also indicate a direction of 180 degrees and 135 degrees respectively; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not indicated for the location north. It is not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So let's deal with the location north then. With respect to the location north, isn't it true that if the angle is precisely 180 degrees that can affect the reception in a way differently than if the angle is, say, 175 degrees or 185 degrees?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. In the case of these antennas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And wouldn't it be reasonable that within the actual corps itself, the unit itself, that identifying a direction as south could be very well sufficient enough to convey a precise direction?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand your question. What am I supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. The direction south that's indicated on the documents that you looked at from the north facility wasn't created for the benefit of you or me or anyone else in here; right? That's an internal document.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the locations south and north. Yes, I believe that this is an internal document. If you want me to talk more precisely about these locations I can go on in order to avoid any confusion. The north location is to the north from the south location.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. What I'm saying is that when the direction south is indicated in a document that was created by the north facility, that that indication is sufficient to convey a specific direction to the people that are in that facility that are doing that job. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were an operator, I would not use that. If I knew the location, I would provide a very accurate orientation of the antenna to the last degree, and then I would have the best reception from that facility if I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Right. So the precision of that angle is important to the ability to receive. Right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very important for the following reason: The diagram of the antenna reception is -- is dependent on the angle, very dependent on the angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Right. And so your analysis of the ability to receive based upon the general direction of south is based upon an assumption of the accuracy of the angle that you looked at, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this comes to the northern site I would say so, yes. If we're talking about north, yes. When it comes to the southern location, they provide very accurate angles there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Those angles that are indicated in the documents from the southern facility correspond to the general directions of south and south-east; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They correspond the way it is indicated. 180 is pure south, 135 degrees is between 90 and 180 degrees, and this is pure, optimum south-east. And I believe they had the same views of the whole situation at the northern situation, but they put things on paper differently. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just bear with me one moment. All right. Could I please have P02827 in e-court. We're not broadcasting, are we? Do you see this document in front of you, this report from the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the southern facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you see a particular azimuth corresponding to the direction, as is indicated, of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Bear with me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm just talking about what's on the screen in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The azimuth is 110 degrees. Just a moment. Let me see. Yes. My azimuth is 113 degrees, 113. I used the data for the southern interception facility towards Vlasenica was 113 degrees and here it is indicated 110, which is very close. I was familiar with the final location of this radio relay station Vlasenica is somewhat broader than what I knew the location to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So it's clear from this document, by the way which is dated the 14th of February, 1995, that the direction, the azimuth, from the southern facility in the direction of Vlasenica is not 135 degrees or 180 degrees; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see 113 in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's not in your analysis and the report which I'm referring to which should be on the --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But that azimuth I didn't find anywhere in the documents that I included in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So this document makes very clear that the southern facility was perfectly aware of the azimuth that corresponded to the direction of Vlasenica from its own position; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could my colleague indicate to us whether this document P2827, first, if this document is on the Rule 65 ter list of documents of the Prosecution and whether this document has ever been disclosed to the Defence and, if so, when the document was disclosed. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can pretty surely say it does not have a 65 ter number. I think it is responding to the direct examination of the witness, and I can say that it was disclosed along with all of the other intercept-related material, and so the Defence has access to that document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm practically certain that this document has never been submitted to us, and I have a small reservation, but I'm practically sure. The worst is that the document does not come from a -- comes from a protected witness and that this document should have given us. It's in the EDS -- it's not in the EDS, in fact, but it's in a general collection, and that has many million documents. So the very fact that it's in this collection doesn't mean that that document has been disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can you be more -- Mr. Bourgon. Before I give you the floor, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd just like to know, Mr. President. I believe this document here that we have was -- we were informed by the Prosecution that they would use this document for cross-examination a couple of days ago. Now, our understanding is that the cross-examination of this witness began long time ago and that all documents to be used in cross-examination should have been given to us at that time and not in the second part of the cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This particular document was on -- was on the list which was the subject of much debate the last time when cross-examination began. That was -- that was the list that was turned over to Defence pursuant to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was already on the list on that occasion, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. There is nothing for us to say if that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Could I have, please, P02822, please, shown to the witness. Could we again turn to ERN number ending 649.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see this document before you, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is another document that was generated by the southern facility back in 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. This is a document that I showed you before, but we can go to the first page if you need to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tell us the number again. 2822?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: English page number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see the date there of November 18, 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the location and the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is there an English translation of this document available?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Yes, it is. I see the assistant --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Of the two relevant pages, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could, could we go back to page ERN ending page 649. Okay. Mr. Rodic, could you just about down to -- that's fine. Mr. Rodic, do you see an indication in that document as to an azimuth relating to Vlasenica from the southern facility of 115 degrees?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's about 2 degrees off from your own calculation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And this document also indicates that the ABiH knew very well what direction from its facility that particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Rodic. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, the Prosecutor just asked a question, and I wanted to know which particular route is included, is involved in this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's indicated on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
